akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿كِتَابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ﴾: "the Book" is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; He informed [by it] that the revelation is a Book. Then He said ﴿فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾: He occupied the verb with "the verses" so that they became like the fāʿil (agent), and He put "Quran" in the accusative.

akhfash:4-5.t: And His word ﴿بَشِيراً وَنَذِيراً﴾ (is accusative) since (the verb) was occupied away from it. If you wish, you make it accusative by way of praise, as though when He turned to praising it He said "We have mentioned an Arabic Quran, a bearer of good tidings and a warner", or "We have mentioned it as an Arabic Quran", and what had preceded of its mention was an indication of what was implied. And He said ﴿وَمِن بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is "and between us and you is a veil", but "مِنْ" came in for emphasis.

akhfash:9-9.t:
As for His word ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ and then His saying ﴿أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾, He means only that this together with the first is four days, just as you say "تَزَوَّجْتُ أَمْسِ امرأةً، واليومَ ثِنْتَيْنِ" (I married a woman yesterday, and today two), one of whom is the one you married yesterday.
He said ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ﴾: He means "with good".

akhfash:10-10.t: As for whoever reads ﴿سَوَآءً لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ﴾ in the accusative, he makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He said "evenly" (اِسْتِواءً). It has also been read in the genitive, made a noun (attribute) for the equal ones, i.e. in four complete days.

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَحِفْظاً﴾, as though He said "and We guarded it with a guarding", because when He said "We adorned it with lamps" He had informed that He looked into its affairs and took care of it, and that indicates guarding; as though He said: "and We guarded it with a guarding".

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ﴾: this is the dialect of those who say "نَحْس", and ﴿نَحِسات﴾ is the dialect of those who say "نَحِس" (ill-omened).

akhfash:21-21.t:
And He said ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾: the wording for them came like the wording for humans, since they were described as speaking and acting, as He said ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمْلُ ٱدْخُلُواْ مَسَاكِنَكُمْ﴾: when they understood and spoke they became like humans in their wording. The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is poetic witness no. 235]:
فَصَبَّحَتْ وَالطَّيْرَ لَمْ تَكَلَّمِ * جَابِيَةً طُمَّتْ بِسَيْلٍ مُفْعَمِ
(She came in the morning, while the birds had not yet spoken, to a cistern filled by a brimming torrent.)

akhfash:26-26.t: And He said ﴿لاَ تَسْمَعُواْ لِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنِ وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾, i.e. do not obey it, as you say "سَمِعْتُ لكَ" (I listened to you, i.e. obeyed you). It is — and Allah knows best — in the sense of "do not listen to the Quran". He said ﴿وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾ because it is from "لَغَوْتُ" "يَلْغَا", like "مَحَوْتُ" "يَمْحا" (to erase). Some read ﴿وَالْغُوا فِيهِ﴾ and said "لَغَوْتَ" "تَلْغُو", like "مَحَوْتَ" "تَمْحُو". Some Arabs say "لَغِيَ" "يَلْغَى", and it is ugly and rare; but (one says) "لَغِيَ بِكَذَا وكَذا", i.e. he became addicted to it, so he keeps saying it and we make it.

akhfash:28-28.t: And He said ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّارُ﴾: nominative as a mubtadaʾ, as though it were an explanation of "the recompense".

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿أَلاَّ تَخَافُواْ﴾: He means "that you should not fear" (بأن لا تخافوا).

akhfash:32-32.t: [And He said] ﴿نُزُلاً﴾ (accusative) because He occupied ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ with ﴿مَا تَشْتَهِيۤ أَنفُسُكُمْ﴾ so that it became like the agent, and it is definite. His word ﴿نُزُلاً﴾ is accusative on the basis of "We have provided it as hospitality", like His word ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾.

akhfash:34-34.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ تَسْتَوِي ٱلْحَسَنَةُ وَلاَ ٱلسَّيِّئَةُ﴾: this may be allowed, because you say "لا يَسْتَوِي عبدُ اللهِ وَلاَ زَيْدٌ" when you mean "ʿAbd Allāh and Zayd are not equal", since both of them together are not equal. If you wish, you say the second (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), meaning: "ʿAbd Allāh and Zayd are not equal"; [lā] was added for emphasis, as He said ﴿لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾, i.e. so that they may know, and as He said ﴿لاَ أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.

akhfash:41-41.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ﴾: some commentators claimed that its khabar (predicate) is ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾. It may also be that it relies on the statements in the Quran, by which it is made self-sufficient, just as some things are self-sufficient without a khabar when the speech is long and the meaning is known, as in His word ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ﴾ and the like. A shaykh among the people of knowledge told me: "I heard ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar ask ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd: '﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ﴾ — where is its khabar?' ʿAmr said: 'Its meaning in tafsīr is: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ﴾ disbelieved in it, ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ﴾.' ʿĪsā said: 'You have hit it, O Abū ʿUthmān.'"

akhfash:44-44.t: And He said ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً أعْجَمِيّاً لَّقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ ءَاعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ﴾: He means ﴿هَلاَّ فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ أَأَعْجَمِيٌّ﴾ (why were its verses not made clear? Is it foreign?) — meaning the Quran — ﴿وَعَرَبِيٌّ﴾ — meaning the Prophet ﷺ. It has been read without interrogation, and both are allowed with one meaning.

akhfash:48-48.t: And He said ﴿وَظَنُّواْ مَا لَهُمْ مِّن مَّحِيصٍ﴾, i.e. and they became certain; because ﴿ما﴾ here is a particle, not a noun, and the verb does not operate on the like of this, so for that reason the verb was made inoperative (mulghā).

daas-irab:1-6.t: ﴿حم﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنَ الرَّحْمنِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to تنزيل. ﴿الرَّحِيمِ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿كِتابٌ﴾ a badal from تنزيل. ﴿فُصِّلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿آياتُهُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب. ﴿قُرْآناً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَرَبِيًّا﴾ naʿt. ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a naʿt of قوم. ﴿بَشِيراً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿وَنَذِيراً﴾ conjoined to it. ﴿فَأَعْرَضَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿قُلُوبُنا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي أَكِنَّةٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قالوا is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to أكنة. ﴿تَدْعُونا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and نا is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَفِي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; في is a preposition. ﴿آذانِنا﴾ a genitive noun; both are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿وَقْرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنْ بَيْنِنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿وَبَيْنِكَ﴾ conjoined to بيننا. ﴿حِجابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَاعْمَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّنا عامِلُونَ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its khabar; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) particle. ﴿أَنَا بَشَرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿مِثْلُكُمْ﴾ naʿt. ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the clause is a second naʿt. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining and restrained particle. ﴿إِلهُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلهٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾ naʿt; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is the nāʾib fāʿil of يوحى [Translator's note: the source prints the particle as إِنَّما, while its analysis treats it as anna (the verse reads أَنَّما)]. ﴿فَاسْتَقِيمُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, its fāʿil being the wāw; the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَوَيْلٌ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-10.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُؤْتُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الزَّكاةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to كافرون. ﴿هُمْ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿أَجْرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿مَمْنُونٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿أَإِنَّكُمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving, reproachful interrogation (istifhām inkārī tawbīkhī), and inna and its noun. ﴿لَتَكْفُرُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna, the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قل is resumptive. ﴿بِالَّذِي﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ both attached to خلق. ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and تجعلون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْداداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿رَبُّ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to جعل. ﴿رَواسِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِها﴾ both attached to an omitted naʿt. ﴿وَبارَكَ﴾ conjoined to جعل. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَقَدَّرَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to قدر. ﴿أَقْواتَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي أَرْبَعَةِ﴾ both attached to قدر. ﴿أَيَّامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿سَواءً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿لِلسَّائِلِينَ﴾ both attached to سواء.

daas-irab:11-13.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اسْتَوى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿إِلَى السَّماءِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿وَهِيَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿دُخانٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the verbal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَها﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَلِلْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to لها. ﴿ائْتِيا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the alif is the fāʿil. ﴿طَوْعاً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿كَرْهاً﴾ conjoined to طوعا; the clause ائتيا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قالَتا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿طائِعِينَ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿فَقَضاهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is latent. ﴿سَبْعَ﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿سَماواتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَوْحى﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي كُلِّ﴾ both attached to أوحى. ﴿سَماءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَمْرَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَزَيَّنَّا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السَّماءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِمَصابِيحَ﴾ both attached to زينا. ﴿وَحِفْظاً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿تَقْدِيرُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْعَلِيمِ﴾ badal (substitute); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and إن is conditional. ﴿أَعْرَضُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of the saying, and the clause فقل is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis. ﴿صاعِقَةً﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِثْلَ﴾ naʿt. ﴿صاعِقَةً﴾ muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: the source prints this second word with the accusative ending; in the verse it is genitive, صاعِقَةِ]. ﴿عادٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾ conjoined to عاد.

daas-irab:14-16.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿جاءَتْهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الرُّسُلُ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to it. ﴿أن﴾ lightened from the heavy (anna) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla). ﴿لا تَعْبُدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) [Translator's note: the source prints the word as أَلَّا; in the verse it is إِلَّا]. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an, its omitted noun and its khabar is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not making the verb jussive. ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿رَبُّنا﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَأَنْزَلَ﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَلائِكَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَإِنَّا﴾ a conjunction, and inna, with نا as its noun (ism). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to كافرون. ﴿أُرْسِلْتُمْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and أما is a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿عادٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of عاد. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مِنَّا﴾ both attached to أشد. ﴿قُوَّةً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause قالوا is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the wāw is a conjunction, and لم is a particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna and the Name of Majesty, its noun. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ naʿt (adjective); the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يروا. ﴿خَلَقَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿هُوَ أَشَدُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of anna, and the verbal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to أشد. ﴿قُوَّةً﴾ tamyīz. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both attached to يجحدون. ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿رِيحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿صَرْصَراً﴾ naʿt. ﴿فِي أَيَّامٍ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿نَحِساتٍ﴾ a naʿt of أيام. ﴿لِنُذِيقَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْخِزْيِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي الْحَياةِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ naʿt. The interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلنا. ﴿وَلَعَذابُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, the lām is for inception (li-l-ibtidāʾ), and عذاب is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَخْزى﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-20.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أما is a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿ثَمُودُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فَهَدَيْناهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَاسْتَحَبُّوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb conjoined to هديناهم. ﴿الْعَمى﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَى الْهُدى﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to استحبوا. ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿صاعِقَةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْهُونِ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to أخذتهم. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَنَجَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿يَتَّقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا. ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) of an omitted verb. ﴿يُحْشَرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿أَعْداءُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلَى النَّارِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُوزَعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of inception (ḥarf ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial and conditional, not making the verb jussive. ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿جاؤُها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. ﴿شَهِدَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿سَمْعُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَأَبْصارُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُمْ﴾ conjoined to سمعهم; the clause شهد is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to شهد. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila.

daas-irab:21-23.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لِجُلُودِهِمْ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِمَ﴾ the lām is a preposition, and ما is an interrogative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām; both are attached to what follows them. ﴿شَهِدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنْطَقَنَا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of الله. ﴿أَنْطَقَ كُلَّ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَوَّلَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿مَرَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to what follows them. ﴿تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿تَسْتَتِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم. ﴿أَنْ يَشْهَدَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿سَمْعُكُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَلا أَبْصارُكُمْ وَلا جُلُودُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to سمعكم. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna and the Name of Majesty, its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظننتم. ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to كثيرا. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَذلِكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿ظَنُّكُمُ﴾ its khabar. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ naʿt. ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَرْداكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of أصبح; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:24-27.t: ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and إن is conditional. ﴿يَصْبِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فَالنَّارُ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and النار is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مَثْوىً﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to مثوى; the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the clause يصبروا is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَإِنْ يَسْتَعْتِبُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَما﴾ a conjunction, and ما is negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ the noun (ism) of ما. ﴿مِنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar of ما; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿وَقَيَّضْنا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿قُرَناءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَزَيَّنُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and زينوا is a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَحَقَّ﴾ a past verb conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿فِي أُمَمٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَالْإِنْسِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of أمم. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانُوا خاسِرِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause قال is resumptive. ﴿لا تَسْمَعُوا﴾ the lā of prohibition (lā al-nāhiya), and an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لِهذَا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْقُرْآنِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative. ﴿وَالْغَوْا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تَغْلِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause gives the reason. ﴿فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause نذيقن is the response to an omitted oath. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿شَدِيداً﴾ its naʿt. ﴿وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ﴾ conjoined to لنذيقن. ﴿أَسْوَأَ﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila of الذي.

daas-irab:28-30.t: ﴿ذلِكَ جَزاءُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿أَعْداءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿النَّارُ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿فِيها﴾ both also attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿دارُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْخُلْدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿جَزاءُ﴾ a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a ḍamma; in the verse it is accusative, جَزاءً]. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to جزاء. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun (ism); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both attached to what follows them. ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause ذلك جزاء is resumptive. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ a munādā (the one addressed) in a genitive construct (muḍāf), and نا is an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَرِنَا﴾ a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter, and نا is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَضَلَّانا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالْإِنْسِ﴾ conjoined to الجن. ﴿نَجْعَلْهُما﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَحْتَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) in the place of the second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَقْدامِنا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِيَكُونا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), and the alif is its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْأَسْفَلِينَ﴾ its khabar; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نجعل. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رَبُّنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اسْتَقامُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَتَنَزَّلُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle forming a maṣdar and making the verb accusative [Translator's note: the source prints the particle as إِنَّ; in the verse it is an (أَلَّا = أن لا), which matches the analysis]. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَخافُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. «قائلين» (saying). ﴿وَلا تَحْزَنُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَبْشِرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِالْجَنَّةِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila.

daas-irab:31-34.t: ﴿نَحْنُ أَوْلِياؤُكُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِي الْحَياةِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to أولياؤكم. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لكم is a fronted khabar. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿تَشْتَهِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿أَنْفُسُكُمْ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِيها ما تَدَّعُونَ﴾ conjoined to the preceding clause, and the i'rab is the same. ﴿نُزُلًا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ غَفُورٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted naʿt of نزلا. ﴿رَحِيمٍ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَحْسَنُ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَوْلًا﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾ both attached to أحسن. ﴿دَعا﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to دعا; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَعَمِلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿صالِحاً﴾ a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّنِي﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and لا is negative. ﴿تَسْتَوِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْحَسَنَةُ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ﴾ conjoined to الحسنة. ﴿ادْفَعْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِالَّتِي﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَإِذَا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and إذا is the idhā of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بَيْنَكَ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿وَبَيْنَهُ﴾ conjoined to بينك. ﴿عَداوَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿كَأَنَّهُ﴾ kaʾanna and its noun. ﴿وَلِيٌّ﴾ its khabar. ﴿حَمِيمٌ﴾ naʿt; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذي.

daas-irab:35-37.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and ما is negative. ﴿يُلَقَّاها﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and ها is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause ما يلقاها is resumptive. ﴿وَما يُلَقَّاها إِلَّا﴾ conjoined to the preceding. ﴿ذُو﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿حَظٍّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَإِمَّا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, إن is conditional, and ما is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿يَنْزَغَنَّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿نَزْغٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause ينزغنك is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَاسْتَعِذْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿هُوَ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿السَّمِيعُ﴾ a first khabar (predicate). ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ a second khabar; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مِنْ آياتِهِ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿اللَّيْلُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالنَّهارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿لا تَسْجُدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition (lā al-nāhiya), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لِلشَّمْسِ﴾ both attached to it; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا لِلْقَمَرِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاسْجُدُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ naʿt. ﴿خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, with a latent fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿إِيَّاهُ﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position, and the clause كنتم is initial and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:38-40.t: ﴿فَإِنِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and إن is conditional. ﴿اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle giving the reason for the omitted apodosis [Translator's note: the source says «للشرط المحذوف», literally "for the omitted condition"], and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of الذين, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿بِاللَّيْلِ﴾ both also attached to the verb. ﴿وَالنَّهارِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْأَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar, and the nominal clause is circumstantial. ﴿وَمِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; من is a preposition. ﴿وَمِنْ آياتِهِ﴾ both attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿أَنَّكَ﴾ anna and its noun (ism). ﴿تَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause ترى is the khabar of anna. ﴿خاشِعَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is adverbial and conditional. ﴿أَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عَلَيْهَا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْماءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اهْتَزَّتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَبَتْ﴾ conjoined to اهتزت. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَحْياها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, with a latent fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَمُحْيِ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the khabar of inna; the nominal clause gives the reason. ﴿الْمَوْتى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both attached to قدير. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of inna. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُلْحِدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي آياتِنا﴾ both attached to يلحدون. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَخْفَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the nominal clause إن الذين is resumptive. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation and reproach, the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُلْقى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the verbal clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿آمِناً﴾ ḥāl; the verbal clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is omitted, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿اعْمَلُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿شِئْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to what follows them. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of inna; the clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause gives the reason.

daas-irab:41-43.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِالذِّكْرِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause); the khabar (predicate) of inna is omitted, its implied form being "هالكون" (will perish); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ temporal, meaning "when" (ḥīniyya). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna, its noun. ﴿لَكِتابٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the khabar of inna. ﴿عَزِيزٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَأْتِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْباطِلُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is a second naʿt of كتاب. ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ حَكِيمٍ﴾ both attached to تنزيل. ﴿حَمِيدٍ﴾ a naʿt of حكيم. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿يُقالُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ما﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِلرُّسُلِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause قيل is the ṣila of ما, and the clause يقال is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَذُو﴾ the shifted lām, and ذو is its khabar; the nominal clause is a badal (substitute) from ما and its ṣila. ﴿مَغْفِرَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَذُو عِقابٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt of عقاب.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and لو is conditional, not making the verb jussive. ﴿جَعَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿قُرْآناً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَعْجَمِيًّا﴾ naʿt (adjective); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَقالُوا﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾ a passive past verb and a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿ءَ أَعْجَمِيٌّ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and أعجمي is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَعَرَبِيٌّ﴾ conjoined to أعجمي. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿هُدىً﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قل is resumptive. ﴿وَشِفاءٌ﴾ conjoined to هدى. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي آذانِهِمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿وَقْرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين, and the clause الذين is resumptive. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿عَمًى﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُنادَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾ both attached [Translator's note: the source does not say to what; presumably to the verb ينادون]. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ a naʿt of مكان.

daas-irab:45-46.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; the lām occurs in the response to the oath; and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا مُوسَى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the response to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَاخْتُلِفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and لولا is a conditional particle not making the verb jussive. ﴿كَلِمَةٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar (predicate) is obligatorily omitted. ﴿سَبَقَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of كلمة. ﴿لَقُضِيَ﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna and its noun (ism). ﴿لَفِي﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿في شَكٍّ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar of inna. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ both attached to شك. ﴿مُرِيبٍ﴾ a naʿt of شك; the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun making the verb jussive (majzūm), mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَمِلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿صالِحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَلِنَفْسِهِ﴾ the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb. ﴿وَمَنْ أَساءَ فَعَلَيْها﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and ما is negative. ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِظَلَّامٍ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and ظلام is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما, which operates like laysa. ﴿لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ both attached to ظلام; the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause وما ربك is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:47-48.t: ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached (mutaʿalliq) to يرد. ﴿يُرَدُّ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عِلْمُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿السَّاعَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative. ﴿تَخْرُجُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿ثَمَراتٍ﴾ genitive in form and nominative in position, the fāʿil (agent) of تخرج. ﴿مِنْ أَكْمامِها﴾ both attached to تخرج; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ ما is negative. ﴿تَحْمِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ أُنْثى﴾ من is a redundant preposition, and أنثى is genitive in form and nominative in position, the fāʿil of تحمل; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تَضَعُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl (circumstantial) excepted from the generality of states (mustathnā min ʿumūm al-aḥwāl), i.e. «مقرونا بعلمه» (accompanied by His knowledge). ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember), and it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُنادِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَيْنَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿شُرَكائِي﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is a second mafʿūl bihi of يناديهم. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿آذَنَّاكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ both attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ شَهِيدٍ﴾ من is a redundant preposition, and شهيد is genitive in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and the clause ضل is conjoined to what precedes it and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَظَنُّوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾ من is a redundant preposition, and محيص is genitive in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause stands in place of the two objects of ظن.

daas-irab:49-50.t: ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْأَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ دُعاءِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْخَيْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إن is conditional. ﴿مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ﴾ a past verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَيَؤُسٌ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and يؤوس is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قَنُوطٌ﴾ a second khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis. ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and إن is conditional. ﴿أَذَقْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ both attached to رحمة; the clause is initial. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة. ﴿ضَرَّاءَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa because it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). ﴿مَسَّتْهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is a naʿt of ضراء. ﴿لَيَقُولَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis; the clause is the response to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِي﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ما is negative. ﴿أَظُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿السَّاعَةَ﴾ its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قائِمَةً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām prepares for the oath, and إن is conditional. ﴿رُجِعْتُ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿إِلى رَبِّي﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لِي﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar of inna. ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿لَلْحُسْنى﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and الحسنى is the postponed noun (ism) of inna; the clause is the response to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, the lām occurs in the response to the omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb, and they are its second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ both attached to the verb, and they are its second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿غَلِيظٍ﴾ a naʿt of عذاب.

daas-irab:51-54.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إذا is adverbial and conditional, not making the verb jussive. ﴿أَنْعَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿أَعْرَضَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَنَأى﴾ conjoined to أعرض. ﴿بِجانِبِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ﴾ a past verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil. ﴿فَذُو﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of the non-jussive condition, and ذو is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw. ﴿دُعاءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَرِيضٍ﴾ naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil; its first mafʿūl bihi is omitted. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; من عند: both attached to the omitted khabar, and its noun (ism) is omitted. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause كان is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), the clause أرأيتم is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قل is resumptive. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿كَفَرْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ﴾ mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (مِنْ); the Quranic word is the interrogative مَنْ]. ﴿أَضَلُّ﴾ khabar; the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi of رأيتم. ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾ both attached to أضل. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي شِقاقٍ﴾ its khabar. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ naʿt; the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿سَنُرِيهِمْ﴾ the sīn is a particle of the future, and an imperfect verb and its first mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿آياتِنا﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي الْآفاقِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to the preceding. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive. ﴿يَتَبَيَّنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after حتى. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar; anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the fāʿil of يتبين. ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the wāw is a conjunction joining to something implied, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the weak letter. ﴿بِرَبِّكَ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and رب is genitive in form and nominative in position, the fāʿil of يكف. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both attached to شهيد. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَهِيدٌ﴾ the khabar of anna; the nominal clause is a badal (substitute) from ربك. ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of alerting and opening (tanbīh wa-istiftāḥ). ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فِي مِرْيَةٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted element, the khabar. ﴿مِنْ لِقاءِ﴾ both attached to an omitted element, a naʿt of مرية. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَلا﴾ an opening particle (ḥarf istiftāḥ). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both attached to محيط. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُحِيطٌ﴾ khabar.

farraa:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾: he says: the Torah and the Gospel do not belie it, and they are [from] before it; ﴿ولا من خلفه﴾: he says: no Book will be sent down after it that belies it.

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا يُقَالُ لَكَ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
He (Allah bless him) was distressed by their belying him, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down upon him: nothing of belying is said to you except as the messengers before you were belied.

farraa:44-44.t:
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: ﴿ءَاعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ﴾.
As a question, and they made the ʿayn sukūn (vowelless); and the exegesis came: "Is this messenger to be an Arab while the Book is foreign (aʿjamī)?" Al-Ḥasan read it without a question: أعجمى وعربى, as though he made it part of their saying, meaning the unbelievers, i.e.: "Why have its verses not been set out in detail, some of them Arabic which the Arab understands, and some foreign which the foreigner understands?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ هُدًى وَشِفَآءٌ﴾.
And some of them read it: "أَعَجَمِىٌّ وعربى", asking a question and relating it to the ʿAjam (non-Arabs).
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: more than one of them narrated to me, [Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and] Mindal, from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha, from Sulaymān ibn Qatta, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: عَمٍ.
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
You say to the man who does not understand what you say: "You are being called from far away," and you say to the quick of understanding: "You certainly take a thing from close by." And it came in the exegesis: it is as though they are being called [from the sky], so they do not hear.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَرَةٍ مِّنْ أَكْمَامِهَا﴾.
The husk of the kufurrā (the palm spathe) is a kimm; and the people of the Ḥijāz read it: ﴿وما تخرج من ثمراتٍ﴾.
His saying: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ آذَنَّاكَ﴾.
This is from the saying of the gods whom they used to worship in this world. They said: "We have informed you that there is not among us any witness to what they said."

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَسْأَمُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ مِن دُعَآءِ ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: "من دعاء بالخير".

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿فَذُو دُعَآءٍ عَرِيضٍ﴾: he says: possessing much supplication; if you describe it with length or with breadth, it is correct.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: [167/a] ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ﴾.
[As for أنه: if you wish, you make أنَّ in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) by repetition (takrīr): "Does it not suffice regarding your Lord that He is Witness over all things?"; and if you wish, you make it nominative (rafʿ), as in your saying: "Does it not suffice regarding your Lord] His witnessing over all things?"; and the nominative is dearer to me.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كِتَابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾.
You make [qurʾānan] accusative by the verb, i.e. its verses were set out in detail thus; and it may be accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment), because the speech is complete at His word (āyātuhu). Had it been nominative as an adjective of "Book", it would have been correct, as He said in another place: ﴿كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَاركٌ﴾. Likewise His words ﴿بَشِيراً ونذيراً﴾ admit what ﴿قرآنا عربيا﴾ admits.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿وَمِن بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ﴾.
He says: between us and you there is a separation in our religion, so work for our destruction; we are working for the same against you. And it is said: work according to what you know of your religion, for we are working according to our religion.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words: ﴿لاَ يُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَاةَ﴾.
The zakāt in this place: Quraysh used to feed the pilgrims and give them water, and they denied that to whoever believed in Muḥammad, Allah bless him; so this was revealed about them. Then He said: and in them there is something greater than this: their disbelief in the Hereafter.

farraa:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَاتَهَا﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "wa-qasama fīhā aqwātahā" ("and He apportioned in it its provisions"): He put in this [land] what is not in that, so that they might live together and trade.
His words: ﴿سَوَآءً لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it in the accusative, and al-Ḥasan in the genitive, making it an adjective of "the days", or, if you wish, of "the four". Whoever makes it accusative makes it connected with "the provisions". It may also be nominative, as if a fresh start, as though He said: "That is equal for those who ask"; He says: for whoever wants to know it.

farraa:11-11.t:
His words: ﴿قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا﴾.
He made the heavens and the earths like two, as in His words: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّماءَ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُمَا﴾, and He did not say "[and what is] between them (pl.)"; had it been so, it would have been correct.
His words: ﴿أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ﴾.
He did not say ṭāʾiʿatayn (feminine dual) nor ṭāʾiʿāt (feminine plural). It was taken to refer to the heavens and those in them. It is also permissible to say, even though they are two: "we have come, willing (ṭāʾiʿīna)", so that they are treated like men since they spoke.

farraa:12-12.t:
His words: ﴿فَقَضَاهُنَّ﴾.
He says: He created them and perfected them.
His words: ﴿وَأَوْحَىٰ فِي كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمْرَهَا﴾.
He says: He placed angels in every heaven; that is its affair.

farraa:14-14.t:
His words: ﴿إِذْ جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلرُّسُلُ مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ﴾.
The messengers came to their forefathers and those who were before them; and "from behind them" — He says: and messengers came to them themselves after those messengers. So the hāʾ and mīm in (khalfihim) refer to the messengers. Or it may refer to them [the people], making "from behind them" mean those [messengers] who were with them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His words: ﴿رِيحاً صَرْصَراً﴾.
A cold [wind] that burns [as] fire burns.
His words: ﴿فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ﴾.
The common people read it heavy, with kasra on the ḥāʾ; some of the people of Medina made it light: (naḥsāt).
He said: [And I heard one of the Arabs reciting:
أبلغْ جذاما ولخما أن إخوتهم * طيا وبهراء قوم نصرهم نِحس
(Tell Judhām and Lakhm that their brothers, Ṭayyiʾ and Bahrāʾ, are a people whose help is ill-omened.)]
This is for whoever makes it heavy; and whoever makes it light bases it on His words: "fī yawmi naḥsin mustamirrin".

farraa:17-17.t:
His words: ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
The reading is with Thamūd in the nominative; ʿĀṣim, the people of Medina and al-Aʿmash read so. But al-Aʿmash used to make Thamūd declinable (yujrī, with tanwīn) throughout the Quran except His words: ﴿وآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ﴾, where he did not give it tanwīn, because it is written without alif. Whoever makes it declinable makes it the name of a man or a mountain, and whoever does not makes it the name of the nation to which he belongs. He said: and I heard one of the Arabs say: "You leave the Banū Asad, and they are eloquent", and he did not make Asad declinable. Whatever names that are [normally] declinable you mean by them the tribe, do not make declinable [Translator's note: the source reads «فلا تحرها», apparently for «فلا تجرها»]; but making them declinable is better in Arabic, like your saying: "Tamīmun came to you in its entirety" and "Qaysun in its entirety"; this is among what is made declinable, and it may be made indeclinable with the same explanation as for Thamūd and Asad.
Al-Ḥasan used to read: "wa-ammā Thamūda fa-hadaynāhum", in the accusative. It is an option, but the nominative is better, because ammā seeks nouns and refuses verbs, so it is like a ṣila for the noun. Had ammā been a particle that may be followed by a noun if you wish and by a verb if you wish, the nominative and the accusative would have been equal, as in His words: ﴿والْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناه مَنازِلَ﴾. Do you not see that the wāw goes with the verb and with the noun? You say: "ʿAbdallāh I struck him, and Zayd I left him", because you say: "and I left Zayd"; so the wāw is acceptable with the verb as it is with the noun. But you do not say: "ammā ḍarabta fa-ʿAbdallāh", as you say: "ammā ʿAbdallāh fa-ḍarabta". And whoever permits the accusative while recognizing this reason [165/ب] says: the natural order of what governs nouns in the accusative is that it precedes them, not that they precede it. And all is correct.
His words: ﴿فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
He says: We showed them the way of good and the way of evil, like His words: ﴿وهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجدينِ﴾: good and evil.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us:] al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Qays related to me from Ziyād ibn ʿIlāqa, from Abū ʿUmāra, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said concerning His words ﴿وهَدَيناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾: good and evil.
Abū Zakariyyā said: And likewise His words: ﴿إنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإمَّا كَفُوراً﴾.
And guidance in another sense is that which is right guidance (irshād), like your saying "We made him happy"; of that are
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّّذينَ هَدَى اللّهُ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾, in much of the Quran.

farraa:19-19.t:
His words: ﴿فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ﴾.
It is from wazaʿtu; the meaning of wazaʿtuhu is: I held him back and restrained him. It has come in the commentary: the first of them are held back for the last of them until they enter the Fire.
He said: and I heard one of the Arabs say: "I will certainly send against you someone who will restrain you (yazaʿukum) and bridle you (yuḥkimukum)" — from the ḥakama (bit-ring) of the riding animal. He said: and Abū Tharwān al-ʿUklī recited to me:
فإنكما إن تُحكِمَانى وترسلا * علىّ غُواة الناس إِيبَا وتضلعاً
(For if you two bridle me and loose the misguided among people upon me, I will refuse and resist.)
This is of that kind. īb is from abaytu and ābā.

farraa:20-20.t:
His words: ﴿سَمْعُهُمْ وَأَبْصَارُهُمْ وَجُلُودُهُم﴾.
"Skin" here — and Allah knows best — is the private part; it is something alluded to, as He said: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لاَ تُواعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا﴾, meaning marriage [intercourse]; and as He said: ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِن الْغَائطِ﴾: al-ghāʾiṭ is the open ground, and what is meant by it is: or one of you has relieved himself.

farraa:22-22.t:
His words: ﴿وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ﴾.
He says: you did not fear that your limbs would bear witness against you so that you would hide from them, and you would not have been able to hide. And it may be by way of reproach (taʿbīr) [Translator's note: or "by way of expression"]: i.e. you did not hide from them.
His words: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن ظَنَنتُمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh, in place of ﴿ولكن ظننتم﴾: "wa-lākin zaʿamtum" ("but you claimed"). zaʿm and ẓann are one in meaning, though they may differ.

farraa:23-23.t:
His words: ﴿وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾.
"dhālikum" is in the position of a nominative by "your thought" [as mubtadaʾ (subject) with khabar (predicate)], and you make "ardākum" in the position of an accusative, as if you said: "That is your thought, ruining you". It is also permissible to make the "ruining" the predicate that governs the nominative, on the view of whoever says: hādhā ʿAbdullāhi qāʾimun [166/ا], meaning "ʿAbdallāh — this one — is standing"; but this is disfavoured. And ardākum may be a fresh start; had it appeared as a noun, it would be nominative, like His words in [Sūrat] Luqmān: ﴿الم، تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتَابِ الْحَكِيمِ، هُدًى ورحمةٌ﴾ — Ḥamza read it so; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "a-alidu wa-anā ʿajūzun wa-hādhā baʿlī shaykhun"; and in [Sūrat] Qāf: ﴿هَذَا مَا لَدَىَّ عَتيدٌ﴾. All of this is as a fresh start; had you intended connection, it would be accusative. He said: and someone recited to me:
مَنْ يك ذا بَتٍّ فهذا بَتِّى * مُقيِّظٌ مصيِّف مُشَتِّى * جمعته من نعجات ست *
(Whoever has a cloak — this is my cloak, for summer, for the hot season and for winter; I gathered it from six ewes.)

farraa:25-25.t:
His words: ﴿وَقَيَّضْنَا لَهُمْ قُرَنَآءَ فَزَيَّنُواْ لَهُم مَّا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾.
[What is before them is] of the affair of the Hereafter: so they said: there is no Paradise, no Fire, no resurrection and no reckoning. And what is behind them is of the affair of this world: they made pleasures attractive to them, and amassing wealth, and abandoning spending in the ways of righteousness; this is what is behind them. So the commentary came. It may also be that what is before them is the worldly affairs they are in, and what is behind them is the affair of the Hereafter.

farraa:26-26.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱلْغَوْاْ فِيهِ﴾.
The disbelievers of Quraysh said it. Abū Jahl said to them: When Muḥammad, Allah bless him, recites the Quran, make idle noise during it — make a din — perhaps he will change [something] or forget, and you will overcome him.

farraa:28-28.t:
His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَآءُ أَعْدَآءِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّارُ﴾, then He said: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الخُلْدِ﴾.
And it is the Fire itself. That is correct: [as] if you said: "The people of Kufa have in it a good abode", the abode being Kufa itself; and it is good when you said [with "the abode"] and "Kufa" — it is the abode — so their two wordings differ. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "dhālika jazāʾu aʿdāʾi Allāhi al-nāru dāru al-khuldi" ("that is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity"); this is clear, with nothing [problematic] in it, because the abode is the Fire.

farraa:29-29.t:
His words: ﴿رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيْنِ أَضَلاَّنَا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنسِ﴾.
It is said: the one of the jinn who led them astray is Iblīs, [and] of mankind Cain (Qābīl), who killed his brother; He says: he was the first of mankind to lay down the practice of going astray.

farraa:30-30.t:
His words: ﴿تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ﴾.
At death, giving them good tidings of Paradise. In our reading it is "allā takhāfū" ("that you should not fear"), and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh "lā takhāfū" ("do not fear") without an, by way of reported speech (ḥikāya).

farraa:35-35.t:
His words: ﴿وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ﴾.
He means: none is granted the repelling of evil with good except one who is patient, or one possessed of a great portion. He made it feminine because "the word" (al-kalima) is feminine; and had He meant "the speech" (al-kalām) [and made it masculine], it would have been correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His words: ﴿وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ﴾.
He says: [if] he turns you away from Our command to you to repel evil with good, then seek refuge in Allah — take refuge in Him.

farraa:37-37.t:
His words: ﴿لاَ تَسْجُدُواْ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلاَ لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾.
He created the sun, the moon, the night and the day; and they are made feminine in His words "khalaqahunna" [166/ب] because every masculine thing other than people and the like is feminine in its plural. You say: "Some garments passed by me, and I bought them (ibtaʿtuhunna)", and "I had mosques, and I demolished them and built them (hadamtuhunna wa-banaytuhunna)". Build [on] this.

farraa:39-39.t:
His words: ﴿ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ﴾.
Its yield increased; and rabat means: it swells, then cracks open for the plants.

farraa:41-41.t:
His words: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ﴾.
It may be asked: where is the predicate (jawāb) of inna? If you wish, you may make it ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾. And if you wish, it is in His words: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ﴾ ﴿لاَّ يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَاطِلُ﴾, so that its predicate is known and therefore left out. This seems the more Arabic of the two explanations and the closer to what has come in the Quran.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
﷽
﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 2] — "تَنْزِيلٌ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿كِتابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3]; this is the view of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is permissible that "تَنْزِيلٌ" be made nominative by "حـم", and it is permissible that it be nominative by implying "هَذا", the meaning being: "This is a revelation from the Mighty, the Merciful", that is: "It is a revelation". ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3] — "قُرْآنًا" is made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "its verses have been made clear as a Quran", that is: "its verses have been made clear in the state of its being gathered as Arabic". ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3], that is: We have made it clear for whoever knows.
﴿بَشِيرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 4] are among its attributes.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَبارَكَ فِيها وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾ — on Tuesday and Wednesday, so the total became four days. That is His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ مِن فَوْقِها وبارَكَ فِيها وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها في أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾, that is: in the completion of four days. ﴿سَواءً لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾ — and "سَواءٍ"; the nominative is also permissible. Whoever reads the genitive makes it an attribute of the days, the meaning being: "in four equal days". Whoever reads the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "they were equal, equally (سَواءً، واسْتِواءً)". Whoever reads the nominative takes it in the sense: "they are equal". And "لِلسّائِلِينَ" is attached to His saying: ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾ — for everyone in need of sustenance; it was said "لِلسّائِلِينَ" (for those who ask) only because everyone seeks sustenance and asks for it. It is also possible that "لِلسّائِلِينَ" means: for whoever asked "In how many [days] were the heavens and the earths created?", so it was said: "The earth was created in four equal days, with no addition and no shortfall", as an answer to whoever asked.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إلى السَّماءِ وهي دُخانٌ فَقالَ لَها ولِلأرْضِ﴾ (the verse) — the meaning of "اسْتَوى" is: He turned to the heaven and directed [His will]. ﴿قالَتا أتَيْنا طائِعِينَ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It was said "طائِعِينَ" rather than "طائِعاتٍ" only because they were treated like beings that reason and discern, as it was said of the stars: ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40]. It has also been said: "they said: we come — that is, we and whoever is in us — willingly". And the meaning of "طَوْعًا أوْ كَرْهًا" is in the sense: "obey what I have commanded willingly", in the position of "obey with obedience, or be compelled with compulsion".

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿فَقَضاهُنَّ﴾: He created them and made them. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما ∗∗∗ داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them are two coats of linked mail which David made, or Tubbaʿ fashioned the ample [mail].)
Its meaning is: "he worked them and made them". ﴿وَأوْحى في كُلِّ سَماءٍ أمْرَها﴾ — it was said: "what sets it right", and it was said: "its angels". ﴿وَزَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِمَصابِيحَ وحِفْظًا﴾ — its meaning is: "and We guarded it with the stars from the eavesdropping of the devils, a guarding". So He said: say, do you disbelieve in the One whose power is this, and assign rivals to Him — that is, idols which you carve with your own hands? ﴿ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ العَزِيزِ العَلِيمِ﴾, that is: the One whose attribute this is, and who has this power, the Lord of the worlds.

zajjaj:13-13.t: Then He said: ﴿فَإنْ أعْرَضُوا﴾, that is: if they do not accept your message after this clarification and affirm the oneness of Allah, ﴿فَقُلْ أنْذَرْتُكم صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صاعِقَةِ عادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾, that is: I have warned you that there will befall you what befell those nations before you that disbelieved.

zajjaj:15-15.t: Then He related the story of their disbelief and the cause of their insolence and their persistence in their misguidance, saying: ﴿فَأمّا عادٌ فاسْتَكْبَرُوا في الأرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الحَقِّ وقالُوا مَن أشَدُّ مِنّا قُوَّةً﴾. So Allah sent upon them a furious wind, and He said: ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا في أيّامٍ نَحِساتٍ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16] — and "نَحْساتٍ" is also transmitted. Abū ʿUbayda said: "الصَّرْصَر" is the one with a violent sound, and it has come in the commentary: the intensely cold one. "نَحِساتٍ" means ill-omened; its singular is "نَحِسٌ"; and whoever reads "نَحْساتٍ", its singular is "نَحْسٌ". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 19]

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿وَأمّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْناهُمْ﴾ — the good [reading] is dropping the tanwīn. It is read "ثَمُودٌ" with tanwīn, and "ثَمُودًا" in the accusative is permissible, by an implied verb which the overt one explains. As for the meaning of "هَدَيْناهم", Qatāda said: "We made clear to them the path of guidance and the path of misguidance." ﴿فاسْتَحَبُّوا العَمى عَلى الهُدى﴾. The preferred choice is the nominative of "ثَمُودُ", as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); this is the view of all the grammarians — preferring the nominative — and all of them allow the accusative.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهم صاعِقَةُ العَذابِ الهُونِ﴾ — "الهُون" is the abasement and disgrace which humiliates them and disgraces them.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أعْداءُ اللَّهِ إلى النّارِ فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾ — "إلى النّارِ" is read with fatḥa on the nūn and full (tafkhīm) pronunciation, and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is "إلى النِّارِ" with imāla (inclination) towards kasra. He prefers that — meaning the kasra — only with the rāʾ, because it is a letter with repetition (takrīr) in it; for that reason Abū ʿAmr preferred the kasra. ﴿فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary: "the first of them are held back for the last of them". Its origin is from "وَزَعْتُهُ", when you restrain him. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said when he took up the judgeship: "People must have restrainers (وَزَعَة)", that is: they must have helpers who restrain people from transgression.
﴿شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهم وأبْصارُهم وجُلُودُهُمْ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 20] — it has come in the commentary that "جُلُودُهم" (their skins) is a euphemism for the private parts; the meaning is: their private parts will testify to their sins.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿وَقالُوا لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدْتُمْ عَلَيْنا قالُوا أنْطَقَنا اللَّهُ﴾, that is: Allah made us witnesses.

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿وَذَلِكم ظَنُّكُمُ﴾ — it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and "أرْداكم" is a second khabar. It is also permissible that "ظَنُّكُمُ" be a badal (substitute) for "ذَلِكم", the meaning being: "and your thought which you thought about your Lord has ruined you". The meaning of "أرْداكم" is: it has destroyed you.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿وَقَيَّضْنا﴾: "and We arranged", from where they did not reckon, ﴿لَهم قُرَناءَ﴾ (the verse). He is saying: they made attractive to them their deeds which they do and witness, and what is behind them, and what they resolve to do.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذا القُرْآنِ والغَوْا فِيهِ﴾, that is: oppose it with speech that is not understood, that speech being idle talk (لَغْو). One says: "لَغا، يَلْغُو، لَغْوًا", and one says: "لَغِيَ، يَلْغى، لَغْوًا", when one speaks idle talk, which is speech that yields nothing and whose reality you do not understand.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿ذَلِكَ جَزاءُ أعْداءِ اللَّهِ النّارُ﴾ — what indicates its nominative is His saying: ﴿فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَذابًا شَدِيدًا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 27]; the meaning is: "that severe punishment is the recompense of the enemies of Allah". "النّار" is nominative, a badal (substitute) for "جَزاءُ أعْداءِ اللَّهِ". If you wish, you may make "النّار" nominative as an explanation, as though it were said: "What is it?" and it was said: "It is the Fire". ﴿لَهم فِيها دارُ الخُلْدِ﴾, that is: they have in the Fire the abode of eternity, and the Fire is the abode itself, just as you say: "you have in this house a house of joy", while you mean the house itself. As the poet said:
أخُو رَغائِبَ يُعْطِيها ويَسْألُها ∗∗∗ يَأْبى الظُّلامَةَ مِنهُ النَّوْفَلُ الزُّفَرُ
(A man of great desires, who gives them and asks for them; from him the generous, burden-bearing one refuses injustice.)

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّنا أرِنا﴾ — with kasra on the rāʾ, and with it made quiescent because of the heaviness of the kasra, as they said "فَخْذٌ" for "فَخِذٌ" (thigh). Whoever gives it kasra follows the original, and the kasra is better, because originally it is "أرْئِنا": the hamza was dropped and the kasra remained as an indication of it; and the kasra is better. The meaning of the verse, according to what has come in the commentary, is that by the two He means the son of Adam, Qābīl, who killed his brother, and Iblīs: Qābīl is of mankind and Iblīs is of the jinn. And the meaning of ﴿نَجْعَلْهُما تَحْتَ أقْدامِنا﴾ is: that they be in the lowest depth.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا﴾, that is: they affirmed the oneness of Allah and were steadfast, acted in obedience to Him and kept to the sunna of His Prophet. ﴿تَتَنَـزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾ as bearers of good news, giving them good news at death and at the time of resurrection, so that the terrors of the Resurrection do not alarm them.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿نُـزُلا مِن غَفُورٍ رَحِيمٍ﴾ — its meaning is: and rejoice in the Garden, in which you will be lodged as a hospitable lodging. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: "نُزُلًا" is accusative in two ways. One of them is that it be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "you will have in it whatever your souls desire; We have lodged it as a lodging".
